### `EntityAction`

One entry of `meta.actions` — the derived capability contract.
EVERY standard op is present; `enabled: false` means the op is
unavailable for everyone (route missing or product-disabled).

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| op | `string` | Operation name — canonical (`list`, `get`, `delete.bulk`, ...) or the
 last path segment for non-standard routes (`change_password`). |
| permissions | `string[]` | Declared non-sentinel permissions, verbatim (OR semantics). |
| sentinel | `EntityActionSentinel` | Sentinel gate when the route declares one instead of real perms. |
| enabled | `boolean` | Visibility flag — false hides the CTA for everyone. |
| endpoint | `EntityActionEndpoint` | The registered route that backs this op — present on every `enabled`
 action, absent when no route exists (`enabled: false`). Consumers
 dispatch writes to the declared endpoint instead of recomputing the
 `/api/v1/entities/{entity}` convention — required for ops living under
 non-standard prefixes (e.g. `/api/v1/auth/users`). |

### `EntityActionEndpoint`

Backing route of an `EntityAction` — emitted by the BE route scan.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| method | `string` | HTTP method of the backing route (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, ...). |
| path | `string` | Full registered API path with `:param` placeholders verbatim
 (e.g. `/api/v1/auth/users/:uuid/restore`). Consumers substitute
 placeholders from the row (`:uuid` ← `meta.uid`). |

### `EntityChangedMarker`

Marker published server-side when an auditable entity is saved.
Stored in Redis with a 5-minute TTL so late-joining clients can see the
most recent change without scanning the audit log.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| entity_type | `string` |  |
| entity_uuid | `string` |  |
| version | `number` | The new `version` after the save. |
| audit_log_id | `number` | The `audit_log_id` of the change (for the GET audit/:auditLogId diff endpoint). |
| changed_by | `string` | user_uuid of the writer. |
| changed_at | `number` | Epoch ms of the save. |

### `EntityMeta`

Static entity meta — the shape every `*.meta.ts` file MUST satisfy.
The schema is CLOSED for authored metas: undeclared properties are
compile errors, so new meta props require extending this type first.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| entity | `string` | Entity name, snake_case singular (e.g. `user_profile`). |
| translation_key | `string` | i18n prefix, snake_case singular — used to build dynamic keys. |
| entities_ns | `string` | Namespace OWNING this entity's label keys — the module's own namespace
(`job` → `job.entities.<translation_key>.*`). Absent → `system`
(BE/core-owned entities keep `system.entities.*`).
This is a READ-side reference declared by the owning module — the
namespace write boundary (see `translation-keys.ts`) guarantees the
keys actually live in that module's `<code>.translations` schema. |
| title_key | `string` | Optional i18n key overriding the canonical page title.
When absent, list/create/edit titles are built from the generic
`system.entities.page_title.{list|create|edit}` templates interpolated
with `system.entities.<translation_key>.{plural|singular}`.
Set only for custom pages needing a bespoke title — CRUD entity metas
must not declare it. |
| uid | `string` | Field key holding the entity primary key (usually `uuid`). |
| display_field | `string` | Canonical display field — the column key identifying the entity's
 human-readable label. Drives first-column/sticky table identity and
 default display resolution. |
| display_name | `string` | Display expression template (`${field}` syntax, dot-paths allowed).
OPTIONAL here: `assembleMeta` materializes it as
`"${" + display_field + "}"` when absent — it is always present in the
served response. Used automatically for edit-page titles; reusable for
comboboxes, lists, chips. |
| actions_overrides | `ActionsOverrides` | Per-op enable overrides — may ONLY toggle `enabled` on route-backed
 ops; a missing route already produces `enabled: false`. |
| columns | `MetaColumn[]` | Entity field dictionary (root-level, transversal). |
| table | `TableMeta` | Table options — omit when the entity has no table page
 (e.g. a self-service form meta). |

### `PresenceDelta`

Delta published on the NATS `presence.{entityType}.{entityUuid}` subject.
Consumed by the BE SSE bridge and forwarded to connected FE clients.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| user_uuid | `string` | The user whose presence changed. |
| action | `PresenceAction` | The action that triggered this delta. |
| entry | `PresenceEntry \| null` | The updated entry (for READING/EDITING/HEARTBEAT), or null (for LEAVE). |
| emitted_at | `number` | Epoch ms of the delta (for dedup / ordering on the FE). |

### `PresenceEntry`

A single user's presence on an entity. Stored in Redis as JSON.
One entry per (entity_type, entity_uuid, user_uuid).

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| user_uuid | `string` |  |
| user_name | `string` |  |
| avatar_color | `string \| null` |  |
| avatar_initials | `string \| null` |  |
| status | `PresenceStatus` |  |
| field | `string` | EDITING only — the field being edited. |
| value | `unknown` | EDITING only — the current draft value of the field. |
| last_seen_at | `number` | Epoch ms of the last signal/heartbeat from this user. |
| edited_at | `number` | Epoch ms of this user's last save on the entity — stamped server-side by
the audit hook when it publishes `EntityChangedMarker` for `changed_by`.
Absent until the user's first save while present. The FE compares it to a
5-minute window (and to the client's own mount time) to render the
"recently saved" affordance. |
| tab_count | `number` | Number of open tabs for this user on this entity (deduped by session_id). |

### `PresenceSignal`

Wire payload for `POST /api/v1/entities/:entity/:uuid/presence`.
Sent by the FE on open, on field focus, on field blur, on heartbeat, and on close.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| action | `PresenceAction` |  |
| field | `string` | EDITING only — the field name being edited. |
| value | `unknown` | EDITING only — the current draft value of the field (full value). |
| loaded_version | `number` | READING / HEARTBEAT — the `version` the client loaded (for staleness detection). |
| session_id | `string` | Tab session id — deduplicates tabs for the same user. FE-generated (uuid). |

### `PresenceSnapshot`

Snapshot returned by `GET /api/v1/entities/:entity/:uuid/presence` and
sent as the initial SSE `snapshot` event on connect.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| readers | `PresenceEntry[]` | Users in READING status (not editing). |
| editors | `PresenceEntry[]` | Users in EDITING status. |
| changed | `EntityChangedMarker \| null` | Most recent server-side change marker, or null if none in the TTL window. |
| current_version | `number` | Current `version` of the entity (read from DB on snapshot build). |

## Types & Enums

### `ActionsOverrides`

Per-op enable overrides — may ONLY toggle `enabled` on route-backed ops.

**Type:** `Record<string, { enabled: boolean }>`

### `ConfigEntry`

Standard Config Table entry.

The BE coerces `value` to its native JS type before serialization:
  - `bigint` → native `bigint` (preserved by ext-json response parsing)
  - `number` → native `number`
  - `money`  → native `number` (amount only; currency is in `type_config`)
  - `secret` → `null` (masked by BE)
  - other    → `string`

Write path: callers send the native type (bigint/number/string); the BE
serializes it to the DB string form via `serializeConfigValue`.

### `ConfigEntryType`

Config value type vocabulary — drives widget selection and validation.
Mirrors the SDK `ConfigType` and the BE `type` column.

- `bigint`: integer values backed by JS `BigInt` (renamed from `integer`)
- `number`: decimal/float values backed by JS `Number`
- `money`:  numeric amount with currency metadata in `type_config`

**Type:** `"string" \| "text" \| "boolean" \| "bigint" \| "number" \| "money" \| "badge" \| "single_select" \| "multi_select" \| "url" \| "secret" \| "json" \| "date" \| "datetime" \| "time" \| "email" \| "phone"`

### `DecimalInput`

Anything coercion functions accept: Decimal, native number, bigint, or a decimal string.

**Type:** `Decimal \| number \| bigint \| string`

### `DeletionFilterMode`

Soft-deletion visibility mode — maps to the `deleted_records` list param
on the wire (`non_deleted` → `EXCLUDED`, `deleted` → `ONLY`,
`all` → `INCLUDED`; absent param means the BE default, currently
`EXCLUDED`).

**Type:** `"non_deleted" \| "deleted" \| "all"`

### `EmitDecl`

One published subject — the ConfigEntry display anatomy mirrored:
`label_key` = short translated display name (primary line), `description_key`
= human description (small secondary line), `subject` = the raw key (mono
line). Both keys point at translations in the EMITTING module's namespace
(`<ns>.events.<name>`); pickers render label + desc + subject.

### `EntityActionSentinel`

Sentinel gates a route may declare instead of concrete permissions.
Values mirror the `Permission` enum in `@primebrick/sdk`.

**Type:** `"_public" \| "_authenticated_user" \| "_authenticated_admin"`

### `EntityMetaResponse`

The served `GET /api/v1/entities/{entity}/meta` response:
static meta + runtime-injected `display_name`, `actions`, `collaboration`.

**Type:** `EntityMeta & { display_name: string; actions: EntityAction[]; collaboration: CollaborationMeta }`

### `FilterCondition`

One WHERE condition of a filter preset — serialized verbatim as a
`filters[i]` entry on the `/list` query string (same vocabulary as
`AdvancedFilter` conditions: field/op/value).

### `FilterOperator`

Filter operators available for advanced filters.

**Type:** `"=" \| "!=" \| ">" \| "<" \| ">=" \| "<=" \| "contains" \| "startsWith" \| "endsWith" \| "BETWEEN"`

### `FilterPreset`

A mutually-exclusive preset filter group rendered as its own control in
the table toolbar (tandem with the deletion-filter group). Exactly one
option is always active — there is no "clear" affordance. Declared in
`meta.table.filter_presets`; example: a `schedule_type` scope selector
(recurring / once / all) on a jobs table.

### `FilterPresetOption`

A single selectable option of a table filter preset.

### `FormFieldPlacement`

One field's placement + policy inside an entity form — PAGE-domain
metadata: it positions a field the ENTITY owns; it never redefines the
field's type or validation (those come from `meta.columns` — class-derived
constraints + authored `format`).

`key` MUST exist in the served `meta.columns` — the host archetype
validates at render time and fails loudly on drift.

### `FormPageDecl`

`page_props.form` — the entity-form page declaration. `fields` is the
ORDERED placement list: only declared keys render (absent columns are
simply not editable on this surface). `validators` names closed-vocab
cross-field rules implemented host-side (e.g. `target_matches_lane`) —
the host rejects unknown validator keys.

### `HostApiFn`

`ctx.components.hostApi` — the host's authenticated full-path fetch
(`apiFetch`): reaches BE-owned `/api/v1/…` endpoints that `ctx.api`
(ws-bound to the owning service) cannot. Remote pages bind it through
`bindRemoteCtx(ctx)` → `getServiceApi('host')`.

**Type:** `(path: string, init: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>`

### `HostMountHandle`

Handle returned by `ModulePageHost.mount_host` — imperative channel to a
host-mounted component root.

### `ListConnector`

Global connector joining the advanced-filter group.

**Type:** `"AND" \| "OR"`

### `LucideRewriteResult`

### `MetaColumn`

Entity field descriptor — the root-level `columns` dictionary.
Transversal to every page type: table cells, form tooltips, labels.

Declared as a type alias (not interface): object literal types get an
implicit index signature, keeping `MetaColumn` assignable to
`Record<string, unknown>` — host/remotes pass columns through generic
cell-snippet args typed as `Record<string, unknown>`.

### `MetaColumnFormat`

Authored field-format vocabulary — the SEMANTIC input contract of a
column: which control archetype a form renderer must use and which
validation chain `buildEntityFormSchema` applies. Absent → the renderer
falls back to `type` (text→text input, boolean→switch, badge→options).

Closed union on purpose: an unknown `format` in a `*.meta.ts` file is a
compile error — the US→FE option boundary is enforced by the type.
New formats are additive literals (never breaking).

**Type:** `"text" \| "textarea" \| "email" \| "url" \| "phone" \| "secret" \| "nats_subject" \| "schedule_spec" \| "json" \| "display_name" \| "idp_name" \| "color_hex" \| "number" \| "money" \| "date" \| "datetime" \| "time"`

### `MetaColumnType`

UI column renderer type. NOTE: this is the UI type, not the DB type —
 e.g. `roles` is `"text"` here but `jsonb` on disk (never ILIKE-searchable).

**Type:** `"text" \| "badge" \| "boolean" \| "color" \| "date" \| "datetime" \| "number" \| "sparkline"`

### `MfaStepUpFn`

`ctx.components.mfaStepUp` — host-bound step-up MFA bridge. The remote
calls it exactly like the host's `useMfaStepUp().executeWithToken`:
`requestFn` runs once with `token = null`; on a `403` response carrying
`mfa_step_up_required` the host shows ITS OWN step-up dialog (host root,
host runtime — nothing crosses the boundary), awaits verification, then
retries `requestFn` with the action-authorization token. The promise
resolves with the final Response — success or failure.

**Type:** `(requestFn: (token: string \| null) => Promise<Response>, context: { action: string; target_resource: string }) => Promise<Response>`

### `ModuleEventsDecl`

### `ModuleHostBase`

Host-side context base handed to EVERY remote mount — pages
(`mountPage`) and sheets (`mountSheet`) alike. Versioned via
`host_version` — remote chunks can refuse incompatible hosts.

HARD CONSTRAINT — plain values and functions ONLY: Svelte rune state
(`$state`/`$derived`/`$effect`) is bundle-local and cannot cross this
boundary. UI building blocks come from `@primebrick/ui` bundled inside
the remote chunk, not from ctx; `components` is reserved for the few
host-coupled cases (see `components` doc).

### `ModuleHostComponents`

`ctx.components` — the reserved well-known keys plus open caller-provided
entries. `remote` is assigned by the host loader after the chunk
resolves; `mfaStepUp`/`openSheet`/`hostApi` are built-ins the host
always provides (a caller may override them in tests).

### `ModuleNavDeclaration`

A module's self-described navigation declaration — the payload a service
publishes in `service.register` (`endpoints.nav`) so the FE can render
the module's sidebar nav and the census can resolve its routes WITHOUT
the BE hardcoding another module's pages. This is the wiring that lets
each module present its own nav — a remote page is owned by the service
that ships it, never declared inside a host module's registry.

`route_prefixes` drive active-module resolution (longest-prefix match —
a page under a shared prefix like `/system/jobs` resolves to the owning
module, not to the module owning the broader `/system` prefix).

### `ModuleNavLink`

One sidebar navigation link contributed by a module. `children` is the
collapsible-group mechanism (the shell renders children under the parent).

### `ModuleNotifyInput`

Notification payload accepted by `ctx.notify` — the minimal shape of the
host's `pushNotification` input. Plain values only.

### `ModulePageHost`

Host ctx handed to a remote page's `mountPage(el, ctx)` — the shared
ModuleHostBase plus the page's own route axis (`nav`/`meta`).

**Type:** `ModuleHostBase & { nav: PageRouteDeclaration; meta: EntityMeta }`

### `ModuleSheetDecl`

A remote sheet panel declared by a service inside `endpoints.nav.sheets`
— the sheet analogue of a remote PageRouteDeclaration: the host
owns the sheet ENGINE (open/close/chrome/state), the owning service owns
the CONTENT — an `esm-mount` chunk exporting `mountSheet(el, ctx)`,
mounted at runtime into the host's global sheet surface.

`key` is the open-sheet address, `<module>.<name>` namespaced so a
declared key can never collide across services (enforced at enrollment
by the nav-declaration validator). Anyone holding the key can open it —
host `openSheet`, `ctx.components.openSheet` — visibility is gated by
the sheet's derived access key (`access.<ns>.<name>`), never by import
reachability.

### `ModuleSheetDefaults`

Chrome defaults a sheet declaration may suggest. The caller's `openSheet`
options always win over these — they are a hint, not a policy.
`content_class` maps to the host engine's `contentClass` option.

### `ModuleSheetHost`

Host ctx handed to a remote sheet's `mountSheet(el, ctx)` — the shared
ModuleHostBase plus the `sheet` control surface: the declared
key, the caller's props (opaque at the boundary — the owning module
knows their shape), the current chrome, and the commands to mutate the
host-owned frame. No `nav`/`meta` — a sheet is not a route; domain
context arrives through `sheet.props`.

**Type:** `ModuleHostBase & { sheet: { key: string; props: Record<string, unknown>; side: ModuleSheetSide; modal: boolean; close: () => void; replace: (props: Record<string, unknown>) => void; setExpanded: (expanded: boolean) => void } }`

### `ModuleSheetSide`

Sheet side — the two chrome slots the host sheet engine owns.

**Type:** `"left" \| "right"`

### `MountPageFn`

The `esm-mount` chunk's entry contract — `export function mountPage(el, ctx)`.
May return the `mount()` result (disposed via `unmount()`), a custom dispose
function, or a promise of either.

NOTE: a raw `mount()` result is only safe when it was registered by the
SAME svelte module instance that will call `unmount()` on it. Remote
chunks resolve svelte through the vendor import map while the host runs
its own bundled copy — two `mounted_components` registries — so chunk
code MUST go through `mountModuleContent` (or return an equivalent
dispose closure over the mounting bundle's `unmount`), never hand the
host a foreign mount record.

**Type:** `(el: HTMLElement, ctx: ModulePageHost) => unknown`

### `MountSheetFn`

The sheet chunk's entry contract — `export function mountSheet(el, ctx)`.
The chunk is declared in `endpoints.nav.sheets[]` (ModuleSheetDecl)
and mounted inside the host's global sheet surface. Same dispose rules as
MountPageFn.

**Type:** `(el: HTMLElement, ctx: ModuleSheetHost) => unknown`

### `OpenSheetFn`

`ctx.components.openSheet` — opens a sheet panel by key: a host-registered
panel (`shell.*`/`entity.*`/`config.*`) or a remote-declared sheet
(`<module>.<name>` from `nav.sheets[]`, mounted at runtime). The panel
registry, remote declarations and sheet state all live in the host — a
remote page requests the panel, it never ships the engine. `props` are
plain values (callback fns are allowed — they cross the boundary);
`options` are the host's sheet options (`side`, `contentClass`, `modal`,
`keepMountedState`). Unknown keys are rejected with a host notification —
the remote cannot smuggle an undeclared panel.

**Type:** `(panelKey: string, props: Record<string, unknown>, options: Record<string, unknown>) => void`

### `PageRouteComponentFormat`

Remote component delivery format. Extensible — new literals are additive
and non-breaking. `esm-mount`: a precompiled ESM chunk that exports
`mountPage(el, ctx)` (or a default component as fallback).

**Type:** `"esm-mount"`

### `PageRouteDeclaration`

One declared frontend route owned by a module. Modules MUST declare every
FE path they own that is not deducible from nav links or entity
conventions — the AI route census (derived from the consolidated
`GET /api/v1/modules` discovery payload) depends on it.
`param` marks dynamic segments using the FE convention ([uuid], [code]).

### `PageRouteKind`

Page archetype vocabulary — what the route renders, regardless of delivery.

**Type:** `"list" \| "detail" \| "create" \| "page"`

### `PageRouteProps`

`page_props` — free-form per-route metadata with a typed `form` axis.

### `PresenceAction`

Client → BE signal describing what the user is doing on an entity.

- `READING`: user opened the entity (loaded_version is what they fetched).
- `EDITING`: user is editing a field (field + value are the current draft).
- `HEARTBEAT`: keep-alive (refreshes the Redis TTL; no state change).
- `LEAVE`: user closed the tab / navigated away.

**Type:** `"READING" \| "EDITING" \| "LEAVE" \| "HEARTBEAT"`

### `PresenceStatus`

Persistent status derived from the latest non-heartbeat signal.
`HEARTBEAT` and `LEAVE` do not change `status` (LEAVE removes the entry).

**Type:** `"READING" \| "EDITING"`

### `RemoteDepsManifest`

`<chunk>.deps.json` — emitted next to each remote chunk at build time,
declaring the vendor specifiers/versions it was compiled against.

### `RoundingMode`

**Type:** `"UP" \| "DOWN" \| "CEILING" \| "FLOOR" \| "HALF_UP" \| "HALF_DOWN" \| "HALF_EVEN"`

### `SnakeCaseSingular`

Branded type that enforces snake_case singular (no uppercase letters).
Used for `translation_key` in entity meta — the i18n key prefix.

The brand is applied via `asSnakeCaseSingular()`, which performs a
runtime check rejecting strings containing A-Z. This catches camelCase
(`userProfile`), PascalCase (`RoleMapping`), and UPPER_CASE
(`USER_PROFILE`) at both compile time and runtime.

**Type:** `string & { __snakeCaseSingularBrand: unique symbol }`

### `SortDir`

Sort direction for server-side list queries and header UI.

**Type:** `"asc" \| "desc"`

### `StandardOp`

**Type:** `typeof STANDARD_OPS[number]`

### `TooltipPriority`

Tooltip visual severity — drives icon and title color in priority
 tooltip renderers.

**Type:** `"INFORMATION" \| "WARNING" \| "ERROR" \| "QUESTION" \| "HINT" \| "SUCCESS"`

### `VendorManifest`

Host `vendor-manifest.json` — specifier → published vendor asset.

**Type:** `Record<string, { url: string; version: string }>`

### `VendorMismatch`

**Type:** `{ specifier: string; kind: "missing"; required: string } \| { specifier: string; kind: "version"; required: string; provided: string }`

### `VendorResolution`

**Type:** `"external" \| "reject" \| "bundle"`

### `VendorSpecifier`

**Type:** `typeof VENDOR_SPECIFIERS[number]`

### `ViewName`

Table view names supported by entity list pages.

**Type:** `"table" \| "cards" \| "cards_list"`

## Constants

### `fromPG`

Alias of `dec()` — parse a PostgreSQL `numeric`/`decimal` text value.

**Type:** `typeof dec`

### `fromString`

**Type:** `typeof dec`

### `fromWire`

Alias of `dec()` — tolerates the `"…d"` wire suffix.

**Type:** `typeof dec`

### `NUMERIC_MIN_SIG_DIGITS`

Minimum significant digits preserved by automatic `div` scale — mirrors
PostgreSQL `NUMERIC_MIN_SIG_DIGITS` (16). See `pgDivScale`.

**Type:** `16`

### `ONE`

**Type:** `Decimal`

### `STANDARD_OPS`

The canonical vocabulary of standard entity ops. Every op is always
present in `meta.actions` — ops whose route is not registered are emitted
with `enabled: false` (explicitly unavailable) instead of being omitted.

**Type:** `readonly ["list", "meta", "get", "create.single", "update.single", "delete.single", "purge.single", "restore.single", "read.audit", "export", "delete.bulk", "restore.bulk", "duplicate.bulk"]`

### `TEN`

**Type:** `Decimal`

### `VENDOR_BLOCKED_PACKAGES`

Packages that MUST NOT be imported raw inside a remote chunk — they are
already served through a sanctioned vendor specifier (e.g. transformers is
vendored behind `@primebrick/ui/vendor/transformers`). A raw import would bundle
a second runtime copy (split caches, split env config) — reject it.

**Type:** `readonly ["@huggingface/transformers", "clsx", "tailwind-merge", "tailwind-variants", "@lucide/svelte", "bits-ui"]`

### `VENDOR_SPECIFIER_PREFIXES`

Open-ended specifier prefixes — everything under a prefix is a sanctioned
vendor specifier without central allowlisting per item. Unlike
VENDOR_SPECIFIERS (one bundle file per specifier), each prefix
maps to a `/vendor/…/` URL directory: the specifier suffix resolves
verbatim after the prefix.

`@primebrick/ui/vendor/lucide/icons/` covers every lucide icon file the
host vendor build emits at `/vendor/icons/lucide/<dist-name>.js` —
remote chunks never resolve icons through a barrel (a barrel would force
the whole catalog on every consumer), they emit one specifier per used
icon. New lucide releases add icons with zero changes to this contract.

**Type:** `readonly ["@primebrick/ui/vendor/lucide/icons/"]`

### `VENDOR_SPECIFIERS`

Closed allowlist of bare specifiers remote chunks may import. A
package's specifiers normally union into ONE bundle file so the browser
dedupes by URL — a single runtime instance is guaranteed. Exception:
`svelte`'s public subpaths (events/reactivity/store/attachments) get
their own files — their export names collide with the internal signal
API (`get`/`derived` exist in both), and a flat union module cannot hold
both. Shared internals still dedupe through the bundler's shared chunks.

**Type:** `readonly ["svelte", "svelte/internal/client", "svelte/internal/disclose-version", "svelte/internal/flags/legacy", "svelte/events", "svelte/reactivity", "svelte/store", "svelte/attachments", "svelte/motion", "svelte/easing", "svelte/transition", "@primebrick/core", "@primebrick/ui", "@primebrick/ui/vendor/transformers", "@primebrick/ui/vendor/clsx", "@primebrick/ui/vendor/tailwind-merge", "@primebrick/ui/vendor/tailwind-variants", "@primebrick/ui/vendor/bits-ui"]`

### `ZERO`

**Type:** `Decimal`

### `defaultSearchGate(trimmed): boolean`

search-gate — canonical "should this search query hit the server" predicate.

Mirrors the backend list-search gate: ≥3 "real" characters, or an escaped
wildcard (`\*` / `\?`) with ≥1 real char. Prevents per-keystroke queries
while still allowing single-char wildcard searches.

Canonical home for both the host FE and remote module pages — the gate
must match the server-side rule byte-for-byte.

may change between versions. The remedy is rebuilding the remote chunk —
a semver-tolerant handshake would only defer an opaque import failure.

### `div(a, b, opts): Decimal`

`a / b`. Without `scale`, the result uses the PostgreSQL `numeric`
division rule (`pgDivScale` — e.g. `1/3` → scale 20, `10/4` → 16), so
Decimal↔DB computations compare equal digit-for-digit. Rounding defaults
to `HALF_UP`. When the true quotient does not terminate at the target
scale the result is flagged `periodic` (`isPeriodic(d)` → true).

  div(1, 3)            // 0.33333333333333333333 — periodic
  div(10, 4)           // 2.5000000000000000
  div(1, 3, 2)         // 0.33
  div(a, b, &#123; scale: 6, rounding: "HALF_EVEN" &#125;)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| a | `DecimalInput` |  |
| b | `DecimalInput` |  |
| opts | `number \| { scale: number; rounding: RoundingMode }` |  |

### `parseDecimal(input): Decimal`

Parse a decimal string into unscaled form.
Accepts: `"12"`, `"-0.5"`, `".5"`, `"5."`, `"1.5e3"`, `"1E-3"`, `"+4"`.
Rejects: `NaN`, `Infinity`, empty strings, hex, non-numeric garbage.
Scale is preserved as written (`"1.230"` → scale 3).

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| input | `string` |  |

### `pgDivScale(a, b): number`

PostgreSQL-faithful result scale for `x / y` (mirrors `select_div_scale`):
`max(16 - 4·qweight, x.scale, y.scale)` — 16 significant digits minimum.
Verified live: `1/3`→20, `10/4`→16, `1.00/8`→20, `2/1`→16, `100/3`→16.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| a | `DecimalInput` |  |
| b | `DecimalInput` |  |

### `resolveVendorSpecifier(specifier): VendorResolution`

How a remote chunk's bundler must treat a bare import specifier. Both the
host vendor build and every module chunk build derive behavior from this
single function so the plane stays deterministic.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| specifier | `string` |  |

### `rewriteLucideBarrelImports(code): LucideRewriteResult`

Remote-build transform: decomposes named imports of the lucide vendor
barrel into one bare specifier per icon — the chunk then carries only
the icons it actually uses. Type imports are stripped (they exist only
for the compiler, which checks the ORIGINAL source pre-transform).

Non-decomposable forms (`import X`, `import * as X`, `export … from`)
throw — the barrel surface cannot survive into an emitted chunk.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| code | `string` |  |
